enforced_dimensions.max_input_bytes: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced on both path.stat().st_size (before reading) and len(data)/len(payload) for bytes/stream/detached-payload sources
enforced_dimensions.max_header_bytes: codec/reader/reader.py and codec/lazy.py -- enforced on the text-header byte span before parsing
enforced_dimensions.max_output_bytes: codec/writer/writer.py and codec/payload.py -- enforced at every serialization exit point (attached header+payload, detached header, detached printf-form header, and each encoded payload buffer)
enforced_dimensions.max_decompressed_bytes: codec/payload.py -- enforced on the declared-shape-derived expected decompressed size before inflating, and again on the actual decoded size after -- a genuine zip/gzip-bomb detector: a compressed payload whose declared shape implies more bytes than the ceiling is refused before decompression begins
enforced_dimensions.max_entries: codec/payload.py -- enforced on the declared axis/dimension count (NRRD's own 'how many sizes does the header declare' equivalent of an entry-count flood guard)

not_applicable_dimensions.max_nesting_depth: NRRD's own header is a flat key/value list with no nested element structure to bound
not_applicable_dimensions.max_compression_ratio: NRRD's own gzip/bzip2 compressed forms are bounded via the declared-shape-vs-actual-decompressed-size comparison (max_decompressed_bytes, checked before AND after inflation), a stronger, shape-aware guarantee than a bare ratio threshold would give -- proven directly by the existing test_a_compressed_bomb_disproportionate_to_the_declared_shape_fails_cheaply

evidence.key_proof: test_element_count_multiplication_is_checked_against_the_decompressed_ceiling and test_a_compressed_bomb_disproportionate_to_the_declared_shape_fails_cheaply both prove the shape-aware decompression-bomb guard rejects hostile payloads cheaply, before full inflation; test_a_legitimate_compressed_payload_matching_the_declared_shape_still_loads proves the same guard does not false-positive on real data; test_resource_limits_are_caller_configurable proves a caller-supplied limits object is honored, not silently replaced by the package's own defaults.
